problem: "The stored type and shape are fixed when the array is made" is wrong for shape, and it contradicts Section 4 of the same chapter, where a.reshape(3,2) changes the shape of the same data. A student will not know which statement to believe.
fix: The dtype and the total number of elements are fixed when the array is made. The shape can be changed later, for example a.reshape(3,2) gives the same six values a new shape of (3,2).

problem: a[0:2, 1:3] is called "a 2 by 2 block of columns 1 and 2". The row part of the slice is never explained, so a student may think both slices act on columns.
fix: a[0:2, 1:3] takes rows 0 and 1 and columns 1 and 2, giving the 2 by 2 block [[2,3],[5,6]]. The first slice chooses rows, the second chooses columns.

problem: The text does not say that the summed axis disappears from the result. a.sum(axis=0) returning length 3 and a.sum(axis=1) returning length 2 can look arbitrary.
fix: Add: the axis you reduce is removed, so summing a (2,3) array with axis=0 gives shape (3,) and with axis=1 gives shape (2,).
